True scientific models are never so simply a dichomotic "true" or "false." Scientific models predict an outcome with statistical certainty based on gathered information and assumptions. Some routementary models of the atom are still used today for predictive purposes despite disagreeing with the whole of our current scientific discovery. The Bohr-Rutherford model of the atom has great utility and validity in cases like chemical bonding where the thing we are trying to predict has a limited scope that does not require us to consider facets of more objectively accurate models from quantum mechanics.

Radiocarbon dating is not a perfect science and has some known obstacles such as 1) man-made c-14 that has been introduced into the environment from nuclear tests and 2) a heavily pivoted assumption that naturally occuring, cosmogenic c-14 production in the upper atmosphere has always been constant.

The bottom line is that a truly scientific mind should reasonably question everything.
